answer: An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the juniper index resolves every citation against the yarrow checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the kernel audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 103 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 103 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
